To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) gender biases in language generation models trained on news articles can be reduced by filtering news articles based on gender representation, (2) gender biases in these models can also be reduced by filtering out news articles that are more biased, and (3) the reduction in bias can be further improved when both filters are used together

(i) training on news articles leads to unintended gender bias in language generation, (ii) this bias is more prevalent when the model is trained on articles from a specific publication, (iii) the bias is more prevalent in articles from publications that have more male authors, and (iv) the bias can be mitigated by training with a more balanced dataset, and by using a more balanced dataset to generate text

(i) gender bias can be detected in news articles and in the language models trained on them, (ii) gender bias is present in the language models even when trained on a balanced dataset, and (iii) gender bias is not present in the language model when trained on a gender-balanced dataset
